arxiv-2006-14271.title: The Holonomy Groupoids of Singularly Foliated Bundles
arxiv-2006-14271.creator: Lachlan Ewen MACDONALD
arxiv-2006-14271.description: Abstract We define a notion of connection in a fibre bundle that is compatible with a singular foliation of the base. Fibre bundles equipped with such connections are in plentiful supply, arising naturally for any Lie groupoid-equivariant bundle, and simultaneously generalising regularly foliated bundles in the sense of Kamber–Tondeur and singular foliations.

arxiv-2104-05919.title: Document-Level Event Argument Extraction by Conditional Generation
arxiv-2104-05919.creator: Sha Li, Heng Ji, Jiawei Han
arxiv-2104-05919.description: Abstract Event extraction has long been treated as a sentence-level task in the IE community. We argue that this setting does not match human information seeking behavior and leads to incomplete and uninformative extraction results. We propose a document-level neural event argument extraction model by formulating the task as conditional generation following event templates.

arxiv-2106-12892.title: Semiring Provenance for Büchi Games: Strategy Analysis with Absorptive Polynomials
arxiv-2106-12892.creator: Erich Grädel ORCID:0000-0002-8950-9991, Niels Lücking, Matthias Naaf ORCID:0000-0002-1099-5713
arxiv-2106-12892.description: Abstract . This paper presents a case study for the application of semiring semantics for fixed-point formulae to the analysis of strategies in Büchi games. Semiring semantics generalizes the classical Boolean semantics by permitting multiple truth values from certain semirings.

arxiv-2110-03507.title: Optimization of the multi-mem response of topotactic redox La 1/2 Sr 1/2 Mn 1/2 Co 1/2 O 3-x
arxiv-2110-03507.creator: W. Román Acevedo 1,2 , M. H. Aguirre 3,4 , C. Ferreyra 1,2 , M.J. Sánchez 1,5 , M. Rengifo 1,2 , C. A. M. van den Bosch 6 , A. Aguadero 6 B. Noheda 7,8 , D. Rubi 1,2
arxiv-2110-03507.description: Abstract Memristive systems emerge as strong candidates for the implementation of Resistive Random Access Memories (RRAM) and neuromorphic computing devices, as they can mimic the electrical analog behavior or biological synapses. In addition, complementary functionalities such as memcapacitance could significantly improve the performance of bio-inspired devices in key issues such as energy consumption.

arxiv-2112-15348.title: Training Recurrent Neural Networks by Sequential Least Squares and the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers
arxiv-2112-15348.creator: Alberto Bemporad
arxiv-2112-15348.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel algorithm for training recurrent neural network models of nonlinear dynamical systems from an input/output training dataset. Arbitrary convex and twice-differentiable loss functions and regularization terms are handled by sequential least squares and either a line-search (LS) or a trust-region method of Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) type for ensuring convergence.

arxiv-2306-16674.title: Online Learning for Robust Voltage Control Under Uncertain Grid Topology Thanks: Manuscript received 17 August 2023; revised 11 January 2024; accepted 15 March 2024. Date of publication 1 April 2024; date of current version 23 August 2024. This work was supported in part by the Caltech Resnick Susta
arxiv-2306-16674.creator: Christopher Yeh, Jing Yu
arxiv-2306-16674.description: Abstract Voltage control generally requires accurate information about the grid’s topology in order to guarantee network stability. However, accurate topology identification is challenging for existing methods, especially as the grid is subject to increasingly frequent reconfiguration due to the adoption of renewable energy.

arxiv-2410-09153.title: Lattice-Matched Multiple Channel AlScN/GaN Heterostructures
arxiv-2410-09153.creator: Thai-Son Nguyen, Naomi Pieczulewski, Chandrashekhar Savant, Joshua J. P. Cooper, Joseph Casamento, Rachel S. Goldman, David A. Muller, Huili G. Xing, Debdeep Jena
arxiv-2410-09153.description: Abstract AlScN is a new wide bandgap, high-k, ferroelectric material for RF, memory, and power applications. Successful integration of high quality AlScN with GaN in epitaxial layer stacks depends strongly on the ability to control lattice parameters and surface or interface through growth. This study investigates the molecular beam epitaxy growth and transport properties of AlScN/GaN multilayer heterostructures.

arxiv-2502-19079.title: Algebraic independence of infinite series † † footnotetext: AMS Class: 11J85, 11J72. † † footnotetext: Key words and phrases: irrationality; infinite series; algebraic number; linear independence of numbers; algebraic independence of numbers.
arxiv-2502-19079.creator: Jaroslav Hančl, Simon Kristensen, Mathias L. Laursen
arxiv-2502-19079.description: Abstract We give conditions on a finite set of series of rational numbers to ensure that they are algebraically independent. Specialising our results to polynomials of lower degree, we also obtain new results on irrationality and ℚ \mathbb{Q} -linear independence of such series.

arxiv-2503-22003.title: Momentum-Space AC Josephson Effect and Intervalley Coherence in Multilayer Graphene
arxiv-2503-22003.creator: Mainak Das and Chunli Huang
arxiv-2503-22003.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mainak Das and Chunli Huang. Electron transport driven by the phase coherence and interference of quantum many-body wavefunctions is a fascinating phenomenon with potential technological significance. Superconductivity, for example, enables dissipationless transport through macroscopic phase twisting. Similarly, in charge-density waves, once the phase degree of freedom—representing the collective position of electrons relative to the lattice—is depinned, it generates characteristic broadband noise and intriguing AC-DC interference patterns.

arxiv-2507-18907.title: Liquid crystal based tailoring of strong coupling in WS 2 \text{WS}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} metasurfaces: Towards reconfigurable quantum photonics
arxiv-2507-18907.creator: Anu Koviloor Manian, Jayasri Dontabhaktuni
arxiv-2507-18907.description: Abstract Strong light-matter interactions in 2D materials have garnered significant interest for their potential in nonlinear optics and quantum photonics. Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), with their robust excitonic responses, serve as promising materials for exploring these interactions. Importantly, tailoring such strong coupling giving rise to tunable quantum and non-linear emissions are under explored.

arxiv-2601-03898.title: Introducing The Maximum Common Bigraph Problem
arxiv-2601-03898.creator: Kyle Burns Michele Sevegnani Ciaran McCreesh James Trimble
arxiv-2601-03898.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Kyle Burns Michele Sevegnani Ciaran McCreesh James Trimble. Bigraph reactive systems offer a powerful and flexible mathematical framework for modelling both spatial and non-spatial relationships between agents, with practical applications in domains such as smart technologies, networks, sensor systems, and biology.

pmc-10573549.creator: Xiaoning Han, Zaiqiang Hu, Liangshu Yu, Yuan Pang, Haicheng She, Longfei Zhang, Xiaoliang Wang, Changjun Qi
pmc-10573549.description: To reveal the dynamic characteristics of asphalt core embankment dams (ACEDs), we carried out a dynamic triaxial experiment on hydraulic asphalt concrete (HAC) under different temperatures (T = 4 °C, 10 °C, 16 °C, and 22 °C) and stress states (Kc = 1.0, 1.2, 1.4, and 1.6; σ3 = 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 MPa).

pmc-10670307.title: Children and Young People with Long COVID—Comparing Those Seen in Post-COVID Services with a Non-Hospitalised National Cohort: A Descriptive Study
pmc-10670307.creator: Fiona Newlands, Anne-Lise Goddings, Maude Juste, Holly Boyd, Manjula D Nugawela, Snehal M Pinto Pereira, Emily Whelan, Elizabeth Whittaker, Terence Stephenson, Isobel Heyman, Trudie Chalder, Emma Dalrymple, CLoCk Consortium, Terry Segal, Roz Shafran, Danilo Buonsenso
pmc-10670307.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: Post-COVID services have been set up in England to treat children with ongoing symptoms of Long COVID. To date, the characteristics of children seeking treatment from these services has not been described. Purpose: (1) to describe the characteristics of children aged 11–17 referred to the Pan-London Post-COVID service and (2) to compare characteristics of these children with those taking part in the United Kingdom’s largest research study of Long COVID in children (CLoCk).

pmc-11516699.title: Covid-19 and mental health hospitalizations in Italy. Results from a multicenter longitudinal cohort
pmc-11516699.creator: A Petrelli, M Ventura, R Ciampichini, A Di Napoli, V Fano, M Pacifici, C Rosini, F Voller, A Zucchi, M Aragona
pmc-11516699.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe impact of Covid-19 pandemic on mental health (MH) is still being assessed. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of Covid-19 on ordinary hospital admissions for psychiatric disorders in Italy.MethodsThe multicenter project “Covid-19 and mental health” (CoMeH), coordinated by the National Institute for Health, Migration and Poverty, enrolled an open cohort of subjects resident in three large areas of Italy (2018-2021) aged 10 + (N = 5,159,363), and followed-up until 2021.

pmc-12373790.title: Ni/NHC-catalyzed C5-H alkylation and alkenylation of challenging furan(thiophene)-2-carboxaldehydes enabled by recyclable imine protecting group
pmc-12373790.creator: Olga V. Khazipova, Oleg V. Khazipov, Konstantin E. Shepelenko, Alexey S. Kashin, Yu Zhang, Victor M. Chernyshev, Valentine P. Ananikov
pmc-12373790.description: Transition-metal-catalyzed C-H alkylation of heteroaromatics with alkenes represents an atom-economical and cost-effective strategy for accessing industrially and pharmaceutically relevant compounds. However, the selective C5-H alkylation of biomass-derived furfural and its isosteric analog, thiophene-2-carboxaldehyde, highly challenging yet industrially vital substrates, has remained elusive.

pmc-12415816.title: Genetic factors associated with the co-occurrence of endometriosis with antiphospholipid syndrome (Review)
pmc-12415816.creator: Maria I. Zervou, Theoni B. Tarlatzi, Demetrios A. Spandidos, Basil C. Tarlatzis, George Bertsias, George N. Goulielmos
pmc-12415816.description: Immune-related factors may serve an important role in the development of endometriosis, considering the occurrence of substantial abnormalities in the immune system of women with endometriosis, including reduced T-cell reactivity and natural killer cell cytotoxicity, as well as increased numbers and activation of peritoneal macrophages.

pmc-13117328.title: Valorization of Spent Brewer’s Yeast by Pulsed Electric Field Treatment Combined with Enzymatic Hydrolysis
pmc-13117328.creator: Valentina Ganeva, Boyana Angelova
pmc-13117328.description: Spent brewer’s yeast, a major by-product of the brewing industry, is a valuable source of bioactive compounds. The main technological limitation for their recovery is the rigid yeast cell wall, while the high nucleic acid content may restrict the direct use of yeast-derived extracts for human nutrition.

pmc-13138002.title: Closing PFAS analytical gaps: Inter-method evaluation of total organofluorine techniques for AFFF-impacted water
pmc-13138002.creator: Fuhar Dixit, Edmund H Antell, Katharine A Faber, Chuhui Zhang, Manmeet W Pannu, Megan H Plumlee, Jean Van Buren, Abraham Doroshow, William CK Pomerantz, William A Arnold, Christopher P Higgins, Graham F Peaslee, Lisa Alvarez-Cohen, David L Sedlak, Mohamed Ateia
pmc-13138002.description: Multiple poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are present in aqueous film-forming foams (AFFF) used for firefighting activities. Currently, no single analytical technique provides a complete accounting of total PFASs or total organofluorine content in AFFF-contaminated samples. To provide insight into the performance of existing methods, we compared ten previously described PFAS measurement techniques.

pmc-13186906.title: Proximal femoral morphometry and its association with hip fracture patterns: a systematic review with meta-analysis
pmc-13186906.creator: Dimitrios Kotzias, Vasileios Giovanoulis, Christos Koutserimpas, George Triantafyllou, Enejd Veizi, Nikolaos-Achilleas Arkoudis, George Tsakotos, Theodore Troupis, Maria Piagkou
pmc-13186906.description: PurposesProximal femoral fractures (PFFs) represent a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the elderly population. Beyond bone mineral density, proximal femoral (PF) and hip joint (HJ) morphometry have been implicated in fracture susceptibility and fracture pattern. However, the relative contribution of individual geometric parameters remains incompletely defined.

pmc-13346764.title: Carbon dioxide concentration alters cyanobacterial carboxysome encapsulation and redox state in Synechococcus sp. PCC 7002
pmc-13346764.creator: Clair A. Huffine, Catherine G. Fontana, Rosanna L. Garris, Colin Sempeck, Jeffrey C. Cameron, Anton Avramov
pmc-13346764.description: Responsible for fixing 25% of carbon dioxide (CO2) globally, cyanobacteria use carboxysomes to house their CO2 fixing machinery. The formation and permeability of the proteinaceous shell of carboxysomes is an area of active study. While necessary in air (0.04% CO2), the shell is not required when cyanobacteria are in high CO2 levels representative of early Earth.

pmc-13672298.title: Prospective observational study of atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel in patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer: JBCRG-C08/ATTRIBUTE
pmc-13672298.creator: Tatsunori Shimoi, Nobuhiro Shibata, Masahiro Kitada, Michiko Tsuneizumi, Mitsugu Yamamoto, Yukinori Ozaki, Yumi Fujimoto, Sayuri Akiyoshi, Naoki Hashimoto, Miki Yamaguchi, Yutaka Yamamoto, Norikazu Masuda, Hiroshi Tada, Takashi Yamanaka, Yuichiro Kikawa, Tetsuhiko Taira, Shizuka Nakagawa, Taizo Taka

The primary outcome was incidence of investigator-assessed adverse events (AEs). Safety and full analysis populations included 149 and 148 patients, respectively; 4.0% of the full analysis population had Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status ≥2 and 7.
